subject: Re: Production latency & error surge after 2.3 quant rollout
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@optibank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@optibank.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike after v2.3 quant rollout

Vanessa —

We started seeing a big spike in end-to-end latency and 502 errors on our payments inference route right after the scheduled model/quant rollout last night. P95 has doubled (from ~180ms to ~420ms) and a few timeouts led to payment retries. We've attached a screenshot and the timeline. This began ~00:45 PST after the deployment. Can you confirm rollback or mitigation? Our ops and fraud teams are getting alerts.

Attached: screenshot_latency_optibank_20281109.png

--
Asha Patel
Head of ML Ops, OptiBank
asha.patel@optibank.com
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@optibank.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 08:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after v2.3 quant rollout

Thanks for flagging Asha — really sorry for the disruption. We're on it.

Immediate plan: I’ve looped in Markus and Irene from the runtime team to look at kernel selection and the quant profile that rolled with v2.3. Markus — can you pull the warm cache stats and the hotpath traces for the OptiBank route (route id: payments/prod) and confirm whether we saw a sudden increase in sequence length or cache misses starting 00:45 PST?

Irene — if this looks like a Q-profile-induced decode slowdown, please list the options (quick rollback to v2.2, model variant fallback, or emergency re-profile). We will follow up with ETA within 30 minutes and keep OptiBank updated.

Vanessa
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after v2.3 quant rollout

Looking at the runtime traces now. Initial findings:
- There is a ~2.3x increase in KV-cache misses on the payments/prod shard starting 00:46 PST.
- Batch sizes dropped (more small batches), latency per token increased due to kernel fallback for a particular attention path introduced in v2.3 qprofile.
- Error pattern: transient 502s correlate with queue saturation on the hotpath backpressure.

I've attached a perf snapshot pulled at 09:12 PST that includes per-GPU scheduler queues and recent kernel callstats. If this is the qprofile, a rollback of the quant profile on the affected pools should recover latency quickly (warm caches permitting).

Attachments: perf_snapshot_20281109.json, rollout_manifest_v2.3.txt

-Markus
Senior SM, Serving Runtime
From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 08:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after v2.3 quant rollout

Thanks Markus — this matches what I see in the kernel selection matrix. Quick recommendation (ranked):
1) Emergency revert quant-profile for the dedicated pools serving OptiBank to the v2.2 Q-profile (fastest recovery).
2) If rollback isn't possible within 15m due to traffic shifting, enable model-variant routing to v2.2 for 100% traffic for payments/prod and scale up warm capacity to reduce cache misses.
3) Start an accelerated re-profile job with the OptiBank sample traces to identify which attention path causes the fallback; this is medium-term (2–4h).

I will run the revert unless there are objections; will coordinate with infra to avoid cache cold-start by warm preloads. CC'ing Marissa and Aditya since this should hit exec/CS for credits and customer communication.

-Irene
Director, Runtime Engineering
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@optibank.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.moreno@optibank.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike after v2.3 quant rollout

Asha — thank you for the quick details and the patience. Our runtime team has identified the likely root cause (quant profile change in v2.3 causing kernel fallbacks and KV-cache churn). We are initiating a rollback of the q-profile for your dedicated pools now; estimated recovery for P95 is 20–40 minutes after rollback completes and caches warm.

We will also put an A/B rule to route new sessions to v2.2 until we finish a targeted re-profile. I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes and confirm when metrics are back to baseline. If you need a customer-side contact for escalation, I'm available on call.

Apologies again — we'll follow up with a postmortem and proposed compensatory credits if the SLA was impacted.

Best,
Vanessa
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Nov 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: OptiBank incident — escalation and credit decision

Quick update for leadership: OptiBank (large payments customer) experienced P95 latency doubling and intermittent 502s after our 2.3 deploy (q-profile change). Runtime team recommends emergency q-profile revert which is in progress (Vanessa confirming).

As a commercial ask: if rolling revert completes but OptiBank still shows customer-visible retries during the window, recommend offering a goodwill credit (TBD amount) and a postmortem + remediation plan. Vanessa — can you capture the affected window and estimated # affected requests so finance/CS can size the credit?

-Marissa
VP, Customer Reliability
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@optibank.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency & error surge after 2.3 quant rollout — rollback complete

Update: rollback completed at 16:12 PST. Early telemetry shows P95 back near baseline (~190ms) and 502s cleared. Warmup period positive — KV-hit rate climbing and batch sizes normalizing. We'll keep monitoring for 4 hours and run the accelerated re-profile using the OptiBank traces offline.

Asha — apologies again for the disruption. We'll share a short postmortem with timeline and remediation plan by EOD tomorrow and list options for additional guardrails (canary stricter gating, qprofile staged rollout, per-customer canary).

-Markus
Senior SM, Serving Runtime
